meaning: to carry on one's back, to shoulder
mnemonic: The back 背 takes the load 負 and the load stays there for the whole of the walk. A child, round the town: せおう.
notes: 負う おう on its own is bearing a responsibility and 肩 かた is the shoulder itself. 背負う is putting a load on your back.
sentence: 街中で子供を背負って歩いた。
sentence_meaning: I carried the child on my back and walked around the town.

mnemonic: Every one of them out in front 前 of you and not a single one missing. The whole family at the table before anybody eats: そろう.
notes: 揃える そろえる is you gathering them up. 揃う is them all being there.
sentence: 朝は家族全員が揃って食事します。
sentence_meaning: The whole family eats together in the morning.

mnemonic: Out 呼 and back in 吸, which is what the word is made of and also what the thing is. Slowly, please: こきゅう.
sentence: ゆっくり呼吸してください。
sentence_meaning: Please breathe slowly.

mnemonic: You make it look true 真 by looking like 似 the thing itself. My daughter does me, and rather too well: まね.
notes: 真似をする is the usual shape for copying somebody.
sentence: 娘はよく私の真似をします。
sentence_meaning: My daughter often mimics me.

mnemonic: The feeling 気 that people 人 have about a thing, which is not a property of the thing at all. That band has it: にんき.
notes: Read ひとけ the same characters mean signs of anybody being about, as in 人気がない, deserted.
sentence: このバンドはとても人気があるよ。
sentence_meaning: This band is very popular.

mnemonic: A person 亻 standing clear of the row so that everybody has to look up at them. A scholar, and a known one: えらい.
notes: Also said to children for behaving well, and used dryly at adults. 素晴らしい すばらしい admires a thing and 有名 ゆうめい is famous as in widely known. 偉い admires a person, and the two do not always go together.
sentence: 彼は偉い学者です。
sentence_meaning: He's a famous scholar.

mnemonic: Everything is packed, the taxi is booked and there is nothing left standing between you and it. Tomorrow, then: いよいよ.
notes: やっと, ようやく and ついに look back at how long it took. いよいよ looks forward at the thing about to happen, and せめて and 少なくとも are at least, which is a floor and not a finish.
sentence: 明日はいよいよ出発の日です。
sentence_meaning: At last we will set off tomorrow.

mnemonic: The figure 象 you are turned to face 対, which is who the thing is aimed at. University students, for this one: たいしょう.
sentence: このアンケートは大学生が対象です。
sentence_meaning: This questionnaire targets university students.

mnemonic: You take the bundle 束, knock it 攵 into correct 正 shape, and only then is it fit to be seen. Collar and tie, before the speech: ととのえる.
notes: 整う ととのう is a thing being in order. 整える is you putting it in order.
sentence: 彼はスピーチの前に服装を整えた。
sentence_meaning: He adjusted his clothes before the speech.

mnemonic: Down into the water 氵 and not coming back up out of it. The boat did exactly that in the river: しずむ.
notes: Also the sun setting, 日が沈む, and a mood going down.
sentence: ボートが川に沈んだ。
sentence_meaning: The boat sank in the river.

mnemonic: On top 上 of the ground 地 rather than under it, which for a train means daylight and a view: ちじょう.
notes: 地下 ちか is the opposite, underground.
sentence: この電車は地上を走ります。
sentence_meaning: This train runs above ground.

mnemonic: A thing 事 with a use 用 attached to it that will not wait until tomorrow. He is out doing them: ようじ.
sentence: 父は用事で出掛けています。
sentence_meaning: My father is out running errands.

mnemonic: Trace the thing backwards and the cause is sitting there at the far end of it. Overwork, in his case: よる.
notes: Three よる in the deck: 夜 night, 寄る dropping in on the way, and this one, written in kana. Attached to a noun as 〜による it means owing to.
sentence: 彼の病気は過労によるものです。
sentence_meaning: His sickness is caused by overwork.

mnemonic: Turned over 反 and facing 対 the other way, which is what being against a thing actually looks like. I am: はんたい.
notes: Also does the opposite as a noun: 反対の方向 is the other direction.
sentence: 私は反対です。
sentence_meaning: I'm against it.

mnemonic: You hold the thing where it is rather than letting it slide, and she is working extremely hard at it. Her youth: たもつ.
notes: 耐える たえる is enduring something coming at you. 保つ is keeping a state from slipping away.
sentence: 彼女は若さを保とうと必死だ。
sentence_meaning: She's desperately trying to retain her youth.

mnemonic: One footstep after another 歴 and somebody sat writing them down 史. I am rather taken with it: れきし.
sentence: 私は歴史に興味があります。
sentence_meaning: I'm interested in history.

mnemonic: A bird over a mountain, which from out at sea is the whole of what you get. Nobody lives on that one: しま.
sentence: その島には誰も住んでいません。
sentence_meaning: Nobody lives on that island.

mnemonic: You had no idea it had got that far with him, because he never once said. Not to that extent: それほど.
notes: そんなに is the everyday version. それほど is a shade more formal and usually takes a negative behind it.
sentence: 彼がそれほど悩んでいたとは知らなかった。
sentence_meaning: I didn't know he was worried that much.

mnemonic: Really 実, and not as a figure of speech either. Last night's concert earned the word: じつに.
notes: 本当に ほんとうに is the everyday truly and 正に まさに confirms that a word fits. 実に is written, and it sits in front of an adjective.
sentence: 昨日のコンサートは実に素晴らしかったよ。
sentence_meaning: Yesterday's concert was truly wonderful.

mnemonic: The heart 心 gripped from above 恐, and what has hold of him is an examination he has not sat yet: おそれる.
notes: 怖い こわい is being scared of a thing in front of you and 恐怖 きょうふ is the terror as a noun. 恐れる is the verb, fearing something that has not happened.
sentence: 彼は受験の失敗を恐れています。
sentence_meaning: He's worrying about failing the exam.

mnemonic: He has not moved an inch and he is not going to, whatever else gets said in the room. His principles, all the way down: あくまで.
sentence: 彼はあくまで自分の主義を通す人だ。
sentence_meaning: He is a person who stands by his principles to the end.

mnemonic: The nose shape put up on a stand, because the original one had been taken away to mean self. Mine itches: はな.
notes: Same reading as 花 はな, flower. The 自 in this one is the old nose character, which is why 自 means self and why you point at yours.
sentence: 鼻がかゆいです。
sentence_meaning: My nose itches.

mnemonic: You take the weight 担 of whatever has landed 当 on you. Sales, in my case: たんとう.
sentence: 私はセールスを担当しています。
sentence_meaning: I'm in charge of sales.

mnemonic: One 片 hand 手 with the other one somewhere else entirely. Driving like that is how people get killed: かたて.
sentence: 片手運転は危ないよ。
sentence_meaning: Single-handed driving is dangerous.

mnemonic: Not much thread and not much power in it yet, which is a small child exactly. She has one at home: おさない.
notes: 若い わかい is young as in not old and stretches into your thirties. 幼い is a small child, and said of an adult it means immature.
sentence: 彼女には幼い息子がいます。
sentence_meaning: She has a young son.

mnemonic: You sit under the roof where it is being handed out and take some of it away with you. Philosophy, at the moment: まなぶ.
notes: 勉強する べんきょうする is studying as work put in. 学ぶ is learning as taking something on, and it is the more formal word.
sentence: 私は哲学を学んでいます。
sentence_meaning: I study philosophy.

mnemonic: Strongly 強 pulled 引, which is being dragged along rather than persuaded. I could not get out of it: ごういん.
sentence: 友人の強引な誘いを断れませんでした。
sentence_meaning: I was not able to decline my friend's pushy invitation.

meaning: to turn up, to roll up (e.g. sleeves)
mnemonic: The hand 扌 rolls 巻 the cloth up out of the way before any of the work starts. Trouser legs first: まくる.
sentence: ズボンのすそを捲って作業をした。
sentence_meaning: I rolled up the leg of my pants and started work.

mnemonic: It gets out through the very thing that was meant to hold it in, and the whole carriage can hear his music: もれる.
notes: 漏らす もらす is somebody letting it out. 漏れる is it getting out on its own.
sentence: 彼のヘッドフォンから音が漏れているね。
sentence_meaning: Sound is leaking from his headphones.

mnemonic: The whole 全 body 体 of it rather than the part sitting in front of you. Eighty per cent of that is done: ぜんたい.
notes: 部分 ぶぶん is a part and 一部 いちぶ is one part of a thing. 全体 is the lot.
sentence: 全体の80パーセントが完成しました。
sentence_meaning: 80 percent of the total was completed.

mnemonic: How far along the scale a thing has managed to get, and his has gone off the end of it: ど.
notes: 程度 ていど is a degree or an extent as a noun. 度 is the unit, and it does temperature and angles too.
sentence: 彼の無神経さは度が過ぎている。
sentence_meaning: His callousness has gone too far.

mnemonic: No feeling 情 to be found anywhere in it, and what you feel instead is embarrassed on their behalf. Not knowing that: なさけない.
sentence: こんなことも知らないとは情けない。
sentence_meaning: It's pathetic that you don't also know this.

mnemonic: The big 太 one coming up over the hill 阝, which is the sun as an object rather than the light off it. High, in summer: たいよう.
notes: 日 ひ is the sun in the everyday sense and also the day. 太陽 is the star itself.
sentence: 夏は太陽がとても高くなります。
sentence_meaning: In the summer, the sun gets very high in the sky.

meaning: to depend on, to take advantage of
mnemonic: You take the sweet 甘 thing that was offered and then a little more, because they let you. Her kindness, and you knew it: あまえる.
notes: There is no English word for it. Leaning on somebody's affection in a way that is expected, and often welcome rather than rude.
sentence: 彼女の親切に甘えました。
sentence_meaning: I depended on her kindness.

meaning: to step on, to tread on
mnemonic: The foot 足 goes down flat on the thing and stays there. The brake, and hard: ふむ.
sentence: 運転手がブレーキを踏んだ。
sentence_meaning: The driver stepped on the brake.

mnemonic: A stamp 印 pressed down and the figure 象 it leaves behind, which is what somebody carries away from meeting you. His was a good one: いんしょう.
notes: 感じ かんじ is how a thing feels to you. 印象 is the mark it leaves, the impression you carry away.
sentence: 彼からいい印象を受けたわ。
sentence_meaning: I got a good impression from him.

mnemonic: Death 死 and a body 体 in the one word, which is precisely as blunt as it sounds. In the park, this morning: したい.
notes: 身体 しんたい is a living body. 死体 is not.
sentence: 公園で死体が見つかったの。
sentence_meaning: A corpse was found in the park.

mnemonic: You hold it up 支 and you hand it out 配, and doing both of those is what ruling amounts to. Fifty years of it: しはい.
sentence: その権力者による支配は50年以上続いたんです。
sentence_meaning: That powerful person continued to rule for over 50 years.

mnemonic: The place 場 the thing actually happened 現 rather than the report written about it afterwards. You cannot go in: げんば.
notes: The word for a site, a scene or the shop floor, and 現場の人 is somebody who does the actual work.
sentence: 事故現場には入れません。
sentence_meaning: You can't enter the accident scene.

mnemonic: Hope 望 cut clean through 絶 with nothing at all on the far side of it. He had got there about life itself: ぜつぼう.
notes: 希望 きぼう is hope. 絶望 is the same idea with the thread cut.
sentence: 彼は人生に絶望していた。
sentence_meaning: He despaired of life itself.

mnemonic: You watch closely enough to work out what has not been said, and what he worked out was that he should run: さっする.
sentence: 彼は危険を察して逃げた。
sentence_meaning: He ran away sensing danger.

mnemonic: From 以 that point and coming 来 forward, the whole stretch of it. Not once since then: いらい.
notes: Same reading as 依頼 いらい, a formal request. 以来 attaches to a time: それ以来, ever since.
sentence: それ以来彼女に会ってない。
sentence_meaning: I haven't met her since then.

mnemonic: Out on the water with nobody rowing and nowhere in particular to be. A small boat, on the lake: ただよう.
notes: Also used of a smell or a mood hanging in the air. 浮かぶ うかぶ is floating as in staying up. 漂う is floating and being carried along with it.
sentence: 小船が湖を漂っています。
sentence_meaning: The boat is drifting on the lake.

mnemonic: The hand 扌 goes in somewhere deep and feels about for whatever is down there. Every country is at it: さぐる.
notes: 探す さがす is looking for a thing you already know you want. 探る is feeling around to find out what there is.
sentence: 各国がテロリストの動きを探っています。
sentence_meaning: Every country is probing for terrorist movements.

mnemonic: The most 最 big 大 there is, which is about as plain as a superlative gets. That is the biggest ship afloat: さいだい.
sentence: これは世界最大の船です。
sentence_meaning: This is the world's largest ship.

mnemonic: You take it down 下 rather than standing there watching it fall. The volume, a little: さげる.
notes: 下がる さがる is a thing coming down by itself. 下げる is you lowering it.
sentence: 少し音量を下げてください。
sentence_meaning: Please turn the volume down a little.

meaning: to be caught, to be arrested
mnemonic: The hand closes, and this time it closes on you. She had been running a long while: つかまる.
notes: 捕まえる つかまえる is you catching somebody. 捕まる is being caught.
sentence: 彼女はついに捕まりました。
sentence_meaning: She was finally caught.

meaning: to be perplexed, to be bewildered
mnemonic: You are stood at the door 戸 and cannot work out which way 惑 to go through it. He asked and she had no idea what to say: とまどう.
sentence: 彼女は突然のプロポーズに戸惑った。
sentence_meaning: She was flustered by the sudden proposal.

mnemonic: You say 言 a reason 訳, and the saying of it is the entire problem. You have rather a lot of them: いいわけ.
sentence: あなたは言い訳が多すぎます。
sentence_meaning: You give too many excuses.

mnemonic: Evidence 証 held up until the thing is clear 明 to every person in the room. His alibi held: しょうめい.
notes: 証拠 しょうこ is the evidence itself. 証明 is proving something with it.
sentence: 容疑者のアリバイが証明されました。
sentence_meaning: The suspect's alibi was proven.
